summary: Reproduces the final text of the draft international standard for the ISO Connectionless-mode Network Protocol, a Network Layer protocol of the OSI model. It can run between end systems or in relay systems, and provides the connectionless network service defined in an addendum to ISO 8348. It replaces RFC 926.

eli5.summary: The OSI family had its own version of IP. This memo is a copy of the official rulebook for how its packets are addressed and passed along.

questions: what is the clnp header format
subtitle: The OSI answer to IP: ISO 8473, the connectionless network protocol, reproduced as an RFC.

tldr.problem: The OSI model needed a network layer protocol that could carry independent datagrams across a mix of different subnetworks, with segmentation, lifetime control and error reporting, without setting up connections first.
tldr.mechanism: CLNP puts a variable-length header in front of each message. It holds a fixed part, source and destination NSAP addresses, an optional segmentation part and optional parameters, and it defines two PDU types: Data (DT) and Error Report (ER).
tldr.outcome: RFC 994 reproduces the final text of DIS 8473 and replaces RFC 926. It is a copy of an ISO standard document rather than an Internet Engineering product.

today: RFC 994 replaces RFC 926, and the unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It reproduces an ISO draft standard, as a record of the OSI connectionless network protocol.

sections.title: What CLNP Is
sections.content:
RFC 994 reproduces the final text of DIS 8473, the ISO draft international standard for the Connectionless-mode Network Protocol (CLNP). It is a protocol of the Network Layer of the OSI model (ISO 7498) and provides the Connectionless-mode Network Service defined in ISO 8348/AD1. It may be used between network-entities in end systems, in relay systems, or both.

The standard specifies procedures for sending data and control information from one network-entity to a peer, the encoding of the protocol data units (PDUs) with a variable-length header, procedures for interpreting the control information, and what an implementation needs to claim conformance.
sections.eli5: CLNP is the way computers in the OSI family hand each other packets, with no phone call to set things up first.

sections.title: Where It Fits and What It Assumes
sections.content:
CLNP is designed for the Subnetwork Independent Convergence Protocol (SNICP) role: it builds a uniform connectionless service over a mixed set of interconnected subnetworks. It assumes an underlying connectionless service, either directly from a connectionless subnetwork or through a Subnetwork Dependent Convergence Function over a connection-mode one. That underlying service must support a service data unit of at least 512 octets. The service it offers is limited to a maximum network service data unit of 64512 octets.

Two subsets exist. The Inactive Network Layer protocol is a null-function subset for when source and destination share a single subnetwork. The Non-segmenting subset simplifies the header when segmentation is never needed, selected by setting the Segmentation Permitted flag to zero.

Addresses are OSI Network Service Access Point (NSAP) addresses, carried in the preferred binary encoding as strings of octets. Entities in routing parameters are named by network-entity titles, which come from the same name space.
sections.eli5: CLNP does not care what road a packet travels on. It just makes sure a packet looks the same whichever road it takes.

sections.title: The Protocol Functions
sections.content:
The standard describes the protocol as a set of functions. PDU composition builds the header and assigns a Data Unit Identifier that must stay unique for the maximum lifetime of the PDU. Lifetime control uses a field counted in units of 500 milliseconds. Every network-entity decrements it by at least one, and more when delay exceeds 500 milliseconds. A PDU whose lifetime reaches zero is discarded.

Segmentation happens when a PDU is bigger than the underlying service allows. It creates Derived PDUs that copy the header, except for the segment length, checksum and segment offset, and never carries fewer than eight octets of user data. Reassembly rebuilds the original, with a timer after which missing segments are given up on and everything is discarded. If the sender sets the Segmentation Permitted flag to zero, nobody may change that for the PDU's lifetime.

Optional functions include padding, security, source routing, recording of route, quality of service maintenance, priority and congestion notification. A header checksum is optional too. If the originator chooses not to use it, the checksum field is zero.
sections.eli5: Each packet has a timer so lost packets do not wander forever, and a big packet can be cut into pieces and glued back together at the end.

sections.title: The PDU Header
sections.content:
Every PDU holds, in order: the fixed part, the address part, the segmentation part if present, the options part if present, and then the data. The fixed part is nine octets. The Network Layer Protocol Identifier is binary 1000 0001 for ISO 8473 and 0000 0000 for the Inactive subset. The Length Indicator gives the header length in octets, up to 254, and the version field is 0000 0001. After that come the lifetime, three flags (Segmentation Permitted, More Segments and Error Report), a five-bit type code, a 16-bit Segment Length and a 16-bit checksum. A checksum of zero means it is to be ignored.

The address part holds a length indicator and value for the destination address, then the same for the source address. The segmentation part, present only when segmentation is permitted, holds a two-octet Data Unit Identifier, a Segment Offset (a multiple of eight) and a Total Length. Options are coded as a parameter code, a length and a value, may appear in any order and must not be duplicated.
sections.eli5: The header is the label on a parcel: what kind it is, how big, how long it may travel, where it is going and where it came from.

sections.title: Discards and Error Reports
sections.content:
A PDU is discarded for reasons such as a protocol violation, a bad checksum, local congestion, an unparseable header, an unreachable or unknown destination, bad source routing, expired lifetime or an unsupported option. When the Error Report flag was set in the original, the network-entity tries to send back an Error Report PDU (type code 00001).

The ER PDU carries a Reason for Discard parameter and at least the whole header of the discarded PDU, plus optionally some or all of its data. Its second octet points at the first octet of the field where the error was found, or is zero if it cannot be localized. No Error Report is generated for a discarded Error Report. The standard notes that not receiving an Error Report does not mean a PDU was delivered correctly.

Reasons for discard are grouped into classes: general, address, source routing, lifetime, PDU discarded for unsupported features, and reassembly.
sections.eli5: If a packet has to be thrown away, CLNP can send a note back to the sender saying what went wrong.

sections.title: Conformance
sections.content:
To conform, an implementation must be able to originate, handle and receive PDUs under the full protocol, not just the Non-segmenting or Inactive subsets. It must also provide the protocol functions of clause 6 and follow the PDU structure and encoding of clause 7. Some functions can be left out depending on the kind of system. For example, a system connected only to subnetworks with the same maximum data unit size does not need to implement segmentation.

The standard does not set timer values. It says timer values should be chosen so that the requested quality of service can be provided.
sections.eli5: To say you follow the rulebook, you must be able to do the whole job, not only the easy parts.

viz.caption: FIXED PART OF THE CLNP PDU HEADER (RFC 994, FIG. 3)

fields.name: Network Layer Protocol Id
fields.desc: Binary 1000 0001 for ISO 8473; 0000 0000 for the Inactive subset.

fields.name: Lifetime
fields.desc: Remaining lifetime in units of 500 milliseconds.

fields.name: Type
fields.desc: 11100 for a DT PDU, 00001 for an ER PDU.

fields.name: Segment Length
fields.desc: Entire length of the PDU in octets, header and data.

fields.name: Checksum
fields.desc: Over the whole header; zero means ignore.
